subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World
central_question: How can we observe, group and protect the diversity of plants and animals by studying their features, habitats and adaptations?
in_scope_units: Nature walk and diversity in plants and animals around us
Biodiversity, interdependence and respectful observation of living organisms
Importance of grouping plants and animals using similarities and differences
Grouping plants as herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers
Leaf venation, root systems and their relationship
Dicot and monocot seeds and the relation among cotyledons, roots and venation
Grouping animals by movement and body parts
Plants and animals in different surroundings and region-specific biodiversity
Adaptations and habitats, including terrestrial, aquatic and amphibian life
Habitat damage, biodiversity loss, conservation projects and sacred groves
banned_topics: Cell structure and microscopic classification of organisms
Taxonomic kingdoms, phyla and scientific nomenclature beyond this chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: All plants with green stems are trees.
known_pitfalls.correction: Trees usually have tall, hard, thick, brown woody stems, while herbs are generally short with soft green stems.

known_pitfalls.claim: Reticulate and parallel venation have no relation to roots.
known_pitfalls.correction: Plants with reticulate venation generally have taproots, while plants with parallel venation generally have fibrous roots.

known_pitfalls.claim: An adaptation is any temporary action performed by an organism.
known_pitfalls.correction: An adaptation is a special feature that enables a plant or animal to survive in a particular region.

known_pitfalls.claim: Biodiversity loss affects only the species whose habitat is damaged.
known_pitfalls.correction: Plants and animals are interdependent, so habitat damage can disturb the wider biodiversity of a region.

recommended_example_progression: Observe and appreciate local biodiversity without disturbing organisms.
Classify plants and connect stem type, venation and roots.
Connect cotyledons with roots and leaf venation.
Classify animals through movement and body parts.
